🚀 NileX Team

We are a team passionate about space exploration, science, and creativity. Our goal is to bring the forgotten stories of NASA's abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars to life through research, storytelling, and innovative ideas.

We are looking for creative and motivated teammates interested in astronomy, research, writing, graphic design, programming, animation, or video editing.

No need to be an expert—just bring your curiosity, passion, and willingness to learn!
summary:
Terra Analog – Earth Analog Sites for Lunar and Martian Exploration

Terra Analog is an interactive scientific project designed to help find and investigate the locations on our planet similar to the geology and environment of the Moon and Mars. The purpose of the project is to help in preparation for space missions by providing researchers and scientists with opportunities to study locations on our planet before sending astronauts to the Moon and Mars.

The project includes a database of 65 Earth analog locations, an interactive 3D globe that allows users to see satellite images and terrain information, and tools that can be used for comparing different locations based on eight scientific criteria. This project includes the description of geological features such as volcanism, impact cratering, erosion by wind, ice and permafrost, and underground locations, and points out the limitations of the comparison in order to provide scientific accuracy.

Using the project's geological data, visualization, and comparison, scientists and astronauts can train, test robots, and conduct research. The significance of the project consists of making planetary exploration research easier, reducing the risks, and turning our planet into a laboratory.
details:
Project Details – Terra Analog

Team Name: NileX

What does the project do and how does it work?

Terra Analog creates a system of interactive tools that help people understand what features of the environments on Earth resemble those of the Moon and Mars. One of the core tools is a database of over 60 real world Earth sites that users can search and view that represent some aspects of the Moon and Mars.

The globe can be interacted with in a 3D view of the Earth with imagery and the elevation of terrain to help users view each location in a 3D context. There are geological features that help each user understand how a particular location relates to either the Moon or Mars. These relationships are given a comparison score that help people understand each location in a particular context and give a critique of each relationship. The system looks at each site from eight dimensions and helps the user understand where each relationship fails to hold up.

This system is built upon three major AI tools for the mission lab.

AI Mission Architect: Creates three part Earth-based mission roadmap steps for any chosen goal or destination.

AI Reality-Gap Analyzer: Assesses the differences between an analog site on Earth and conditions on a real planetary site.

AI Terrain Scorer: Examines the fit of different terrains to the objectives of any given planetary exploration mission.

2. Interactive games and mission simulations

The platform features more games to spice up the space and planetary learning.

Analog Radar: A scavenger hunt-style mission, Analog Radar lets the player travel around the world, across diverse geological settings to find different analog mission beacons.

Rover Mission Rehearsal: A driving simulator where users play through a mission as an astronaut operating a rover in a realistic analog site.
